```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

`gloss` captures an R figure at draw time—while the graphics engine and R
session are still alive—and packages its dual SVG representation, Engine IR
(data tables, scale/palette dictionaries, layer recipes, facet panels, and
draw-time ordering), structural lineage, and runtime provenance into open,
cross-language files.

## 1. Capturing a Figure Once

```{r capture-grid}
library(gloss)

g <- grid::grobTree(
  grid::rectGrob(width = 0.6, height = 0.4, name = "panel_box",
                 gp = grid::gpar(fill = "#eef6fa", col = "#0072B2")),
  grid::textGrob("Hello gloss", name = "panel_title")
)

cap_grid <- gloss(g, width = 5, height = 3.5)
cap_grid
```

When `ggplot2` is installed, `gloss()` runs a single
`ggplot_build()` -> `ggplot_gtable()` -> `grid.draw()` pass so even stochastic
layers (such as `geom_jitter()`) stay aligned across `original.svg`,
`scene.svg`, and `built_layer*` tables:

```{r capture-ggplot, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ am) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("4" = "#0072B2", "6" = "#E69F00", "8" = "#D55E00"),
    labels = c("4 cyl", "6 cyl", "8 cyl")
  ) +
  labs(title = "Fuel Economy by Transmission", x = "Weight (1000 lbs)", y = "MPG")

cap <- gloss(p)
cap
```

## 2. Inspecting the Asset Map and Slicing in Memory

`gl_asset_map()` builds a lightweight JSON-ready catalog without redrawing the
plot, and `gl_query()` slices leaves, elements, lineage, and panel-filtered
tables directly in memory:

```{r inspect-query, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
map <- gl_asset_map(cap)
str(map$ir$panels, max.level = 2)

# Slice strictly to panel P2 (am == 1) and high-MPG cars
q <- gl_query(cap, panel = "P2", rows = function(df) df$y > 25)
q
head(q$tables$built_layer1[, c("_row_id", "PANEL", "x", "y", "colour")])
```

## 3. Exporting a Portable Open Asset Bundle

`gl_asset_bundle()` writes a self-contained `.gloss/` directory (or `.zip`
archive) with SHA-256 verification in `manifest.json`, explicit column schemas
in `tables/schema.json`, and 1-based `_row_id` keys on every CSV table:

```{r bundle, eval = requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)}
bundle_path <- gl_asset_bundle(
  cap,
  path = file.path(tempdir(), "mtcars.gloss"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)
sort(list.files(bundle_path, recursive = TRUE))
```

## 4. Capturing Base R Figures

Base graphics functions and `recordedplot` objects are captured automatically
via step-by-step display-list replay:

```{r base-capture}
cap_base <- gloss(function() {
  graphics::par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
  graphics::plot(datasets::mtcars$wt, datasets::mtcars$mpg, pch = 16, main = "Scatter")
  graphics::hist(datasets::mtcars$mpg, col = "grey80", main = "Histogram")
})
cap_base
```
